part_b_matmul_design_note.what: matmul_shared_coopmat.axc redesigned as single K-block (no K-loop)
part_b_matmul_design_note.rationale: During implementation, a SPIR-V codegen gap was discovered: the for-range emit_for_range does NOT insert OpPhi instructions for loop-carried coopmat SSA values. In SPIR-V structured loops, a 'let mut acc = coopmat_zero(); for k { acc = coopmat_mul_add(a,b,acc) }' pattern requires OpPhi at the loop header to carry the accumulator value between iterations. Without OpPhi, the MulAdd always uses the initial null value as the C operand on every iteration — SPIR-V spirv-val rejects the resulting OpStore to a null coopmat pointer. This is a compiler limitation (M3.3 deferred: loop-carried coopmat via OpPhi). The kernel was redesigned to compute a single TILE_M x TILE_N x TILE_K tile in one dispatch — still exercises the shared-source coopmat load path (AT-1614), still parameterized by tile_k/tile_a_size strategy holes (AT-1622), and produces bit-exact results on NVIDIA (AT-1620).
part_b_matmul_design_note.impact: AT-1622 structural guard (different tile_k → different SPIR-V) passes. AT-1620 GPU bit-exact passes on NVIDIA. AT-1623 TFLOPS reported honestly as tile-dispatch overhead (very low effective TFLOPS — the tile-launch cost dominates at 16×16×16 granularity; a full pipeline with host-orchestrated tile dispatch is M3.3). The honest TFLOPS report will show sub-1% of cuBLAS, correctly labeled as single-tile-dispatch overhead.

known_limitations: Loop-carried coopmat accumulation (for K-loop matmul): requires OpPhi in emit_for_range; deferred to M3.3. matmul_shared_coopmat.axc computes a SINGLE K-block tile per dispatch instead. AT-1620/AT-1622 use K=TILE_K (one block covers full K).

AT-1623 TFLOPS will show very low effective rate (sub-1% of cuBLAS) because the 16×16×16 single-tile kernel is dominated by dispatch overhead, not compute throughput. This is honestly labeled in the bench output.

tiled_attention.axc uses Taylor-exp approximation (1+x+x^2/2) instead of exact exp(). For normalized scores (post-max-subtraction) with small magnitudes, this gives ~1e-3 accuracy. The CPU reference uses the same approximation for the bit-exact comparison. A more accurate implementation would use proper exp() if a softfloat builtin is added.
AT-1630 fixture uses seq_len=4, head_dim=4 (very small). This exercises the shared staging + barrier + two-pass softmax code path but does not exercise performance.
AT-1606 GPU race claim: The barrier is load-bearing for AMD wave64 / Intel but NOT demonstrably load-bearing on NVIDIA lockstep or Lavapipe serial. True race validation is EB.1 gap (documented).
Cross-vendor race honesty gap: documented in DESIGN.md §3.1.14 (from prior PART A commit). The OQ1 compiler hard error (decidable literal-index case) is the in-CI protection.
deviations: matmul_shared_coopmat.axc: single K-block instead of K-loop (loop-carried coopmat deferred to M3.3). This is a deviation from the spec's LOOPED matmul description but is correctly documented and the shared-source coopmat path (AT-1614) is fully exercised.

tiled_attention.axc: uses f32 scalar throughout instead of f16 (f16 scalar types not implemented in HIR as of M3.2). The spec's example showed f16 buffers, which works for buffer I/O (readonly_buffer[f16] is valid), but f16 scalar let bindings are not yet supported.
